title: YouTube
summary: Video at planet scale: resumable uploads into object storage, a parallel transcoding DAG that produces many bitrates and segments, CDN delivery with adaptive bitrate streaming, and approximate-then-exact view counting.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Upload videos (up to hours long); watch on any device; search; comments; likes; view counts
Uploads processed in minutes; never lose an upload
Billions of views/day; 500+ hours uploaded per minute

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Storage and egress dominate. Transcoding is the compute-heavy batch job, and delivery is a CDN problem with adaptive bitrate on the client.

POST /v1/uploads                 { title, size, mime }     -> { uploadId, resumableUrl }
PUT  {resumableUrl}  Content-Range: bytes 0-8388607/…   (chunked, resumable)
GET  /v1/videos/{id}              -> metadata + manifest URL
GET  {cdn}/{id}/manifest.mpd      -> DASH / HLS manifest
GET  {cdn}/{id}/720p/seg_00042.m4s
POST /v1/videos/{id}/views         (beacon)

head: Data
Key
Store
rows: Sharded MySQL via Vitess (YouTube built Vitess)

blocks.caption: Upload once, transcode in parallel, serve from the edge

items: Client uploads in resumable chunks to object storage; upload service records progress.

On completion, an event enqueues a processing DAG: validate → split into GOP-aligned chunks → encode each chunk × each rendition in parallel → package into HLS/DASH segments → thumbnails, captions, content ID checks.
Metadata flips to PUBLISHED when the minimum renditions exist (low bitrates first, 4K later).
Viewer fetches manifest, then segments from the nearest edge, switching bitrate per segment.
Split long videos into chunks (~a few seconds, GOP-aligned) so thousands of workers encode one video in parallel.
Renditions ladder: 144p … 4K, codecs H.264 / VP9 / AV1; popular videos get extra-efficient encodes later (AV1 costs more CPU, saves bandwidth).
DAG orchestration with retries per task; idempotent tasks keyed by (video, chunk, rendition).
Priority: fast low-quality renditions first so the video is watchable quickly.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: Parallelize across chunks and renditions, publish the cheap renditions first, and re-encode the popular head with better codecs later.

sections.title: Deep dive: delivery and adaptive bitrate

items: HLS/DASH: manifest lists renditions; video is 2–6 s segments; the player picks the next segment's bitrate from measured throughput and buffer level.
Edge caches inside ISPs (Google Global Cache) serve the popular head; the long tail comes from regional caches or origin.
Prefetch the first segments of likely next videos (watch-next).
Signed URLs and per-region rights enforcement at the edge.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Players buffer a few segments and choose bitrate per segment; that, plus ISP-level caches, is how start time stays under two seconds.

items: Billions of increments a day on hot keys: never `UPDATE videos SET views = views + 1`.
Clients send view beacons → Kafka → stream aggregation per video per minute → sharded counters; displayed count is cached and lags slightly.
Fraud filtering: dedupe by user/session, bot detection before counts are final (why counts sometimes freeze).
For a single viral key, use sharded sub-counters (`views:{id}:{0..63}`) summed on read.

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Multi-region storage, CDN failover, client retries other edges
Content ID fingerprint matching in the pipeline

items.title: HLD
items.text: Upload → object store → transcode DAG → renditions → CDN.

items.title: Deep dives
items.text: Chunked parallel transcode, ABR delivery, view counting.

items.q: How do you support live streaming?
items.a: Ingest RTMP/SRT, transcode in real time into short segments (low-latency HLS/DASH), publish manifests every segment.
Candidate generation (embeddings, watch history) → ranking model → re-ranking for diversity, cached per user session.

items.q: How do you reduce storage cost?
items.a: Tier cold videos to cheaper storage, drop rarely used renditions and regenerate on demand.

items: Resumable chunked uploads to object storage.
Transcode DAG: split → encode chunks × renditions in parallel → package.
Publish low bitrates first.
HLS/DASH segments + ABR player.
ISP edge caches for the head, origin for the tail.
Views: beacons → Kafka → aggregate → sharded counters.
